extracted.intended_audience: general readers, Stephen King fans, aspiring writers and students of literature
extracted.subtask_description: Extracted craft guidance and evaluative commentary about fiction-writing drawn from a Stephen King biography/Wikipedia article. Covers King's own maxims (reading/writing, description), critics' standards (realism, characterization, coherence), and exemplars (dialogue, sense of place).

rubrics_metrics.name: Read a lot and write a lot
rubrics_metrics.description: King's basic maxim: "read a lot and write a lot."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as foundational practice advice: consistent, high-volume reading and writing to develop skill. No scoring guidance; framed as essential ongoing habit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good description: clear seeing to clear writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Good description "begins with clear seeing and ends with clear writing, the kind of writing that employs fresh images and simple vocabulary."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes observation and the use of fresh imagery and simple diction. King cites influences (Chandler, Hammett, Ross Macdonald, T. S. Eliot, William Carlos Williams) and specific image examples (Eliot's 'those ragged claws...', Williams' 'white chickens, red wheelbarrow...') as models of compact, vivid description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compact, descriptive language
rubrics_metrics.description: Respect for the power of compact, descriptive language as a craft value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: King credits writers (detective fiction authors and modernist poets) for teaching the effectiveness of compact, precise description; implies favoring economy over purple prose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of homage/retelling in modern context
rubrics_metrics.description: Deliberately pay homage to classic works by retelling or riffing on them in a modern setting (e.g., Salem's Lot vs. Dracula; Revival vs. Frankenstein).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: King describes an intentional literary strategy—using a classic as a 'wall' to bounce his modern story off of—indicating that successful homage reinvents or reframes older material rather than merely copying it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Realistic detail and social eye
rubrics_metrics.description: Bring reality to genre fiction through realistic detail and a 'careful and caring social eye.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jeffery Deaver praises King's ability to infuse genre novels with believable, socially aware details; this is presented as a value that elevates popular fiction toward seriousness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rich characterization and interplay of story and character
rubrics_metrics.description: Use rich characterization and ensure interplay between storyline and character development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deaver notes that the interplay of story line and character development is a distinguishing quality; implies that character actions should drive plot and vice versa, creating mutual reinforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depict the everyday with small, moving details
rubrics_metrics.description: Portray everyday life and small emotional details that create depth (King's 'genius is for the everyday' and 'an eye for the kind of small but moving details').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mendelsohn's praise frames effective horror/popular fiction as equally about ordinary human yearning and small, resonant particulars—not only about supernatural elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ear for authentic dialogue
rubrics_metrics.description: Capture authentic, often coarse, American dialogue—'a deadly ear for the way people speak.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: David Foster Wallace highlights King's skill at realistic dialogue; guidance implies prioritizing natural speech patterns and regional/character-appropriate voice to enhance verisimilitude.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sense of place and evocative atmosphere
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a strong sense of place—poetic evocation of landscape, history, and inhabitants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joyce Carol Oates praises King's saturation of fiction with Maine atmosphere; guidance: use setting as an active, evocative element that shapes mood and character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid bloated, illogical plotting and maudlin tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Criticisms of earlier work: described as 'bloated, illogical, maudlin and prone to deus ex machina endings.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: S. T. Joshi's critique serves as anti-patterns to avoid: strive for leaner prose, logical coherence, emotional restraint (avoid excessive sentimentality), and plausible resolutions rather than deus ex machina. Joshi notes King has been improving in these respects since Gerald's Game.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentence-level craftsmanship and literary focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Attention to sentences, literary focus, and depth—writing that is 'not glib... not just contemporary chatter and it's not stupid.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cynthia Ozick's appraisal emphasizes sentence craft and literary awareness; the criterion suggests valuing careful sentence construction and engagement with literary tradition even in popular fiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be an omnivorous reader
rubrics_metrics.description: Read widely across genres and periods—King describes himself as 'an omnivore' moving from John Sandford to D. H. Lawrence to Cormac McCarthy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages broad reading to inform range, voice, and technique; implies cross-genre learning enhances one's craft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical, unpretentious guidance on craft
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide practical, observant, and unpretentious writing advice (On Writing described as 'the most practical and unpretentious writer's manual around' and compared to Strunk & White).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Valuing clear, useful craft advice aimed at improving day-to-day writing practice rather than theoretical or pretentious claims; suggests prioritizing actionable techniques and clarity.
